subject.title: Dashboard: widget write-back — a setState bridge capability + persisted widget state

question: Should dashboard widget write-back proceed with an approved SQLite/plugin-state storage design and bridge-level security contract, or should maintainers accept a named JSON-state exception for this stack?
rationale: This changes both persistent runtime state ownership and the iframe-to-parent sandbox boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent storage/security direction.

options.title: Require storage and bridge design
options.body: Proceed after the feature uses approved SQLite/plugin-state storage, preserves per-widget isolation and capability gating, and has adversarial tests plus live proof.

options.title: Approve a named exception
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept per-widget JSON state and the current write-back boundary as intentional product debt before continuing review.

options.title: Defer behind the dashboard stack
options.body: Hold the issue until the base dashboard PRs merge or close, then revisit only the write-back delta.

recommendation.title: Require storage and bridge design
recommendation.body: Proceed after the feature uses approved SQLite/plugin-state storage, preserves per-widget isolation and capability gating, and has adversarial tests plus live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the adjacent current-main plugin-tab seam and have the strongest current-main routing signal for the Control UI/plugin boundary.
